old_caption: The video captures a controlled burn on a grassy hillside. The fire actively spreads across the dry, brown grass, creating a vivid contrast against the blue sky. In the foreground, a person in a yellow safety vest walks toward the fire, likely a firefighter or burn manager. The camera angle suggests it is mounted on the head of another individual, providing a first-person perspective. As the video progresses, the fire continues to advance, consuming more of the grass. Several other individuals, also in yellow vests, are scattered across the hill, some standing still while others appear to be moving, possibly managing the burn or observing its progress. A wooden structure, possibly a viewing platform, is visible in the background. The sky remains clear and bright throughout, indicating favorable weather conditions for the burn. The overall atmosphere is one of controlled activity, with the fire being managed rather than uncontrolled.
original_wisa_caption:
The video captures a dramatic scene of a controlled burn on a grassy hillside. The fire is actively spreading across the dry, brown grass, creating a vivid contrast against the blue sky. In the foreground, a person wearing a yellow safety vest is seen walking towards the fire, likely a firefighter or a burn manager. The camera angle suggests it is mounted on the head of another individual, providing a first-person perspective.

As the video progresses, the fire continues to advance, consuming more of the grass. Several other individuals, also wearing yellow vests, can be seen scattered across the hill, some standing still while others appear to be moving, possibly managing the burn or observing its progress. A wooden structure, possibly a viewing platform or part of a fire station, is visible in the background, adding context to the location.

The sky remains clear and bright throughout the video, indicating favorable weather conditions for the burn. The overall atmosphere is one of controlled activity, with the fire being managed rather than uncontrolled
caption: The video captures a dry golden hillside where a curved line of flame is already burning across the slope, its front creeping slowly through the tall grass and leaving a band of blackened, charred earth behind it. A separate foreground flame band flickers continuously along the lower edge, staying active throughout the excerpt. The fire advances gradually rather than erupting, consuming the pale vegetation as it moves across the open ground. A single crew member in a yellow helmet stands on the mid-slope near the flames, drifting rightward as the camera shifts, and remains visible throughout. Several silhouetted figures hold roughly fixed positions along the upper ridge and on the elevated wooden boardwalk at the right, yet slide within the view. The camera pans and tilts gradually, drawing the platform toward the upper-right corner while more of the left ridge and sky enter view. A dark, out-of-focus object at the right edge and a hazy smudge at the lower-right stay fixed relative to the frame, consistent with a helmet-mounted camera obstruction. The scene is viewed through this shifting perspective.

Write a corrected WISA-style training caption for this exact video clip.
This clip is a temporally cropped excerpt, with arbitrary start and end boundaries. It is NOT
necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
